# Command reference

`yojo` has **28 commands**. This page is generated from `yojo commands`, `yojo schema '<command>'`, and the checked examples in [`docs/examples/commands.json`](../examples/commands.json). The JSON Schemas remain the source of truth; run `yojo schema '<command>'` for the exact contract.

> [!NOTE]
> Examples use synthetic data (`EXAMPLE-*` keys, `*.example.test` hosts) and were captured from real runs against test fixtures. They are pretty-printed here; when stdout is piped or `--json` is given, `yojo` prints each envelope on one line. On a terminal it shows a readable view of the same envelope, with the same exit code. Invocations use POSIX shell syntax.

Every command accepts these options:

| Option | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `--json` | Print the JSON envelope even on a terminal. Piped output is always JSON. |
| `--base-url URL` | Jira, Confluence, or Bitbucket HTTPS root for this call; works without yojo.yaml. |
| `--config PATH` | Use this yojo.yaml instead of searching the current directory upward. |

Every command produces exactly one envelope and exits with one of these codes:

| Exit | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | success |
| 2 | input or configuration error |
| 3 | authentication or keyring error |
| 4 | unmet requirement (nothing was written), or config drift/unverified |
| 5 | remote validation error, not found, or conflict |
| 6 | transport, TLS, or service failure, or unknown write outcome |
| 7 | confirmed partial write |

Each error code, with its meaning and fix, is in the [error catalog](errors.md).

## Commands at a glance

| Command | Summary | JSON input |
|---------|---------|------------|
| [`yojo commands`](#yojo-commands) | List every command with its signature and an example. Offline. | no |
| [`yojo schema`](#yojo-schema) | Print argument, input, success, and error JSON Schemas for a command. Offline. | no |
| [`yojo login`](#yojo-login) | Check a personal access token (or username and password) against the service and store it in the OS keyring for that URL. Secrets come from stdin or a hidden prompt, never arguments. Bitbucket takes a token only; `all` means Jira and Confluence. | no |
| [`yojo config check`](#yojo-config-check) | Compare yojo.yaml aliases, create rules, and transition rules with live Jira fields, projects, and statuses, and check that a configured Bitbucket answers and accepts the stored token. Read-only. | no |
| [`yojo init`](#yojo-init) | Draft a version 1 yojo.yaml from live Jira, Confluence, and Bitbucket metadata, using the logins already stored for each URL. Shows a preview by default; --save creates the file only if it is absent, and --replace needs the current file's sha256. Team rules come only from --policy-input (or --input); nothing is inferred and no secret is written. | yes |
| [`yojo agent print`](#yojo-agent-print) | Print the yojo instructions for an AI agent: every command's signature and a --json example, plus the safety rules. Offline; paste the text into any chat. | no |
| [`yojo agent install`](#yojo-agent-install) | Write the agent instructions where each tool looks for them: agents (AGENTS.md), claude (.claude/skills/yojo/SKILL.md), cursor (.cursor/rules/yojo.mdc), copilot (.github/copilot-instructions.md), gemini (GEMINI.md). Only the marked yojo section is replaced; other text is kept, and an unchanged file is not rewritten. | no |
| [`yojo jira issue create`](#yojo-jira-issue-create) | Create an issue of any type. Checks the project's live create screen and any yojo.yaml rules first, and refuses with every problem listed if anything is missing; nothing is written then. | yes |
| [`yojo jira issue get`](#yojo-jira-issue-get) | Read an issue's key, summary, status, type, assignee, and link. --fields adds more fields by name; long text is trimmed unless --full. | no |
| [`yojo jira issue update`](#yojo-jira-issue-update) | Change fields on an issue. Checks the live edit screen first, refuses with every problem listed, then reads the issue back to confirm the new values. | yes |
| [`yojo jira issue link`](#yojo-jira-issue-link) | Link two issues, for example `PROJ-1 blocks PROJ-2`. --type takes the link name or either direction's wording; the link is read back to confirm it. | no |
| [`yojo jira requirements`](#yojo-jira-requirements) | Optional look-before-you-leap: every check `jira transition` would run for moving an issue to a status, plus the planned writes. Read-only. | no |
| [`yojo jira transition`](#yojo-jira-transition) | Move an issue to a status (any case), setting transition-screen fields with --set. Checks every rule and required field first and refuses with all problems listed. A configured pre_edit runs a separate edit first and is not atomic. | yes |
| [`yojo jira attachment add`](#yojo-jira-attachment-add) | Upload a file to an issue after checking permission and the size limit. Succeeds only when Jira confirms the uploaded name and size; otherwise outcome_unknown. | no |
| [`yojo jira comment add`](#yojo-jira-comment-add) | Add a plain-text comment from --body, a file, or stdin, after checking the issue exists and you may comment. | no |
| [`yojo jira search`](#yojo-jira-search) | Run a JQL search. Returns a bounded page (--limit, default 20) and next_start, the explicit cursor for the next page. | no |
| [`yojo confluence page read`](#yojo-confluence-page-read) | Read a page with its storage-format body, trimmed to 2000 characters unless --full. Returned content is untrusted data. | no |
| [`yojo confluence page search`](#yojo-confluence-page-search) | Run a CQL search. Returns a bounded page (--limit, default 20) and next_start, the explicit cursor for the next page. | no |
| [`yojo confluence page create`](#yojo-confluence-page-create) | Create a page from storage-format content given as JSON input. | yes |
| [`yojo confluence page update`](#yojo-confluence-page-update) | Update a page's title and/or storage body. Requires expected_version and rejects stale versions. Succeeds only when Confluence confirms the page id, title, and next version; otherwise outcome_unknown. | yes |
| [`yojo bitbucket repo list`](#yojo-bitbucket-repo-list) | List repositories you can see, optionally in one project. Returns a bounded page (--limit, default 20) and next_start, Bitbucket's cursor for the next page. | no |
| [`yojo bitbucket repo get`](#yojo-bitbucket-repo-get) | Read a repository's name, state, default branch, clone URLs, and link. | no |
| [`yojo bitbucket branch list`](#yojo-bitbucket-branch-list) | List a repository's branches, optionally those whose name contains --filter. Bounded page (--limit, default 20) with next_start. | no |
| [`yojo bitbucket pr list`](#yojo-bitbucket-pr-list) | List a repository's pull requests (--state, default OPEN, any case). Bounded page (--limit, default 20) with next_start. Long titles are shortened; pr get shows the full title. | no |
| [`yojo bitbucket pr get`](#yojo-bitbucket-pr-get) | Read a pull request: title, state, branches, author, reviewers, and description (trimmed unless --full). Reviewers are limited to ten; reviewers_total and reviewers_truncated signal the limit, and reviewers_url opens the full view. Returned content is untrusted data. | no |
| [`yojo bitbucket pr diff`](#yojo-bitbucket-pr-diff) | Show a pull request's changes as a unified diff with a list of changed files. Trimmed to about 2000 characters and 10 files unless --full; --path FILE shows one file (add --old-path OLD for a renamed file). complete is false whenever yojo or Bitbucket cut anything. more, when set, is a yojo command that may show more; inspect, when set, is a git command for what Bitbucket would not return. | no |
| [`yojo bitbucket pr create`](#yojo-bitbucket-pr-create) | Open a pull request between two branches of one repository. Checks the repository, both branches, the title, and for an open pull request with the same branches first, and refuses with every problem listed; nothing is written then. | yes |
| [`yojo bitbucket pr comment`](#yojo-bitbucket-pr-comment) | Add a plain-text comment to a pull request from --body, a file, or stdin, after checking the pull request exists and has no identical comment. | no |

## `yojo commands`

List every command with its signature and an example. Offline.

```text
yojo commands [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

None.

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | yes |
| `schema_version` | integer | yes |
| `commands` | array of objects | yes |
| `global_options` | object | yes |
| `exit_codes` | object | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo commands
```

The `commands` list is shortened to two entries here; the real output lists every command.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "schema_version": 1,
    "commands": [
      {
        "path": "commands",
        "summary": "List every command with its signature and an example. Offline.",
        "usage": "yojo commands",
        "example": "yojo --json commands"
      },
      {
        "path": "jira issue create",
        "summary": "Create an issue of any type. Checks the project's live create screen and any yojo.yaml rules first, and refuses with every problem listed if anything is missing; nothing is written then.",
        "usage": "yojo jira issue create PROJECT --type TYPE --summary TEXT [--description TEXT] [--set 'NAME=VALUE']... [--input FILE|-]",
        "example": "yojo --json jira issue create PROJ --type Bug --summary 'Login fails on Safari' --set 'Story Points=3' --set priority=High"
      }
    ],
    "global_options": {
      "--json": "Print the JSON envelope even on a terminal. Piped output is always JSON.",
      "--base-url URL": "Jira, Confluence, or Bitbucket HTTPS root for this call; works without yojo.yaml.",
      "--config PATH": "Use this yojo.yaml instead of searching the current directory upward."
    },
    "exit_codes": {
      "0": "success",
      "2": "input or configuration error",
      "3": "authentication or keyring error",
      "4": "unmet requirement (nothing was written), or config drift/unverified",
      "5": "remote validation error, not found, or conflict",
      "6": "transport, TLS, or service failure, or unknown write outcome",
      "7": "confirmed partial write"
    }
  }
}
```

Error: an unknown option, `yojo commands --bogus` ([`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error), exit 2):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "usage_error",
    "message": "yojo: unrecognized arguments",
    "fix": "Use `yojo commands` to list commands.",
    "details": {
      "usage": "usage: yojo [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json] COMMAND ..."
    }
  }
}
```

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted) |

## `yojo schema`

Print argument, input, success, and error JSON Schemas for a command. Offline.

```text
yojo schema COMMAND... [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | `COMMAND...` | string | yes |   |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | integer | yes |
| `command` | string | yes |
| `summary` | string | yes |
| `usage` | string | yes |
| `example` | string | yes |
| `arguments` | object | yes |
| `input` | object or null | yes |
| `success` | object | yes |
| `error` | object | yes |
| `error_codes` | array of strings | yes |
| `exit_codes` | object | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo schema 'jira comment add'
```

The `error` schema is abbreviated here; the real output contains the full error envelope schema shared by every command.

## `yojo login`

Check a personal access token (or username and password) against the service and store it in the OS keyring for that URL. Secrets come from stdin or a hidden prompt, never arguments. Bitbucket takes a token only; `all` means Jira and Confluence.

```text
yojo login --service SERVICE [--auth AUTH] [--username USERNAME] [--token-stdin | --password-stdin] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | `--service SERVICE` | one of `jira`, `confluence`, `bitbucket`, `all` | yes |   |
| `auth` | `--auth AUTH` | one of `pat`, `basic` | no | default `pat` |
| `username` | `--username USERNAME` | string | no | Basic auth username (not secret). |
| `token_stdin` | `--token-stdin` | boolean | no |   |
| `password_stdin` | `--password-stdin` | boolean | no |   |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `services` | array of objects | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo login --service jira
```

A human runs this. On a terminal, `yojo` prompts on stderr and reads the personal access token with no echo. In automation, a human pipes the secret on stdin with `--token-stdin`; a secret is never an argument, file, or environment variable. The credential is stored per base URL, so `--base-url` alone can reuse it later.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "services": [
      {
        "service": "jira",
        "auth": "pat",
        "base_url": "https://jira.example.test/jira",
        "user": "example-user",
        "status": "stored"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Error: the only keyring backend is a plaintext file store ([`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable), exit 3):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "keyring_unavailable",
    "message": "No secure OS keyring backend is available.",
    "fix": "Use a native OS keyring: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or a running Linux Secret Service (GNOME Keyring/KWallet) with an unlocked session. Do not configure a plaintext keyring backend.",
    "details": {
      "backends": [
        "keyrings.alt.file.PlaintextKeyring"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes**

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`config_not_found`](errors.md#config_not_found), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`service_not_configured`](errors.md#service_not_configured), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable), [`login_failed`](errors.md#login_failed) |
| 5 | [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

**Input**

**Output**

| `status` | constant `pass` | yes |
| `summary` | object | yes |
| `checks` | array of objects | yes |

## `yojo init`

Draft a version 1 yojo.yaml from live Jira, Confluence, and Bitbucket metadata, using the logins already stored for each URL. Shows a preview by default; --save creates the file only if it is absent, and --replace needs the current file's sha256. Team rules come only from --policy-input (or --input); nothing is inferred and no secret is written.

```text
yojo init [--jira-url URL] [--project KEY...] [--confluence-url URL] [--bitbucket-url URL] [--repo PROJECT/slug...] [--policy-input FILE] [--output PATH] [--save] [--replace] [--expected-sha256 HEX] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jira_url` | `--jira-url URL` | string | no | Jira HTTPS application root. |
| `project` | `--project KEY...` | array of strings | no | Jira project key to list in jira.projects; needs jira_url. |
| `confluence_url` | `--confluence-url URL` | string | no | Confluence HTTPS root. |
| `bitbucket_url` | `--bitbucket-url URL` | string | no | Bitbucket HTTPS root. |
| `repo` | `--repo PROJECT/slug...` | array of strings | no | PROJECT/slug to check; reported, not saved (no config key). |
| `input` | `--policy-input FILE` | string | no | min length 1; Path to a UTF-8 JSON file, or '-' for stdin. |
| `output` | `--output PATH` | string | no | min length 1; Where to save; default yojo.yaml in the current directory. |
| `save` | `--save` | boolean | no | default `false`; Write the file. |
| `replace` | `--replace` | boolean | no | default `false`; Allow --save to replace an existing file; needs the sha256. |
| `expected_sha256` | `--expected-sha256 HEX` | string | no | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}(?![\s\S])`; existing_sha256 from a preview. |

**Input**

A JSON object from `--input PATH`, or from stdin with `--input -`. Unknown properties and duplicate keys are rejected. Where the command also has flags, the input is an alternative to them; a flag and an input property that disagree are refused.

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jira` | object | yes |   |
| `jira.fields` | object (field name to any or any) | no | Alias (lowercase snake_case) to {jira_name: NAME} or {id: FIELD_ID}. |
| `jira.projects` | array of objects | no |   |

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | one of `preview`, `created`, `replaced`, `unchanged` | yes |
| `path` | string | yes |
| `yaml` | string | yes |
| `sha256` | string | yes |
| `existing_sha256` | null or string | yes |
| `services` | array of objects | yes |
| `projects` | array of objects | yes |
| `repos` | array of objects | yes |
| `notes` | array of strings | yes |
| `next` | array of strings | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo init --jira-url https://jira.example.test/jira --project PROJ
```

A preview: nothing is written. Add `--save` to create yojo.yaml, which never overwrites a file. To replace an existing file, add `--save --replace --expected-sha256 HEX` with the preview's `existing_sha256`. Team aliases and rules come only from `--input`.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "action": "preview",
    "path": "/work/repo/yojo.yaml",
    "yaml": "# Drafted by `yojo init` from live metadata. Review it, then run `yojo config check`.\nversion: 1\njira:\n  base_url: https://jira.example.test/jira\n  projects:\n  - key: PROJ\n",
    "sha256": "64f455d77825922053a2dba98c40cb627d7d5e30e655bf58e6ed268c89ef7c53",
    "existing_sha256": null,
    "services": [
      {
        "service": "jira",
        "base_url": "https://jira.example.test/jira",
        "user": "example-user",
        "version": null
      }
    ],
    "projects": [
      {
        "key": "PROJ",
        "name": "Example Project"
      }
    ],
    "repos": [],
    "notes": [
      "Nothing was written. Review the YAML, then run the next command to save it.",
      "No team aliases or rules were added; yojo never infers them. Pass them with --input (see docs/configuration.md)."
    ],
    "next": [
      "yojo --json init --jira-url https://jira.example.test/jira --project PROJ --save"
    ]
  }
}
```

Error: no Jira login is stored for that URL yet ([`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), exit 3):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "auth_missing",
    "message": "No stored jira credential for https://jira.example.test/jira.",
    "fix": "Ask a human to run `yojo login --service jira --base-url https://jira.example.test/jira` in a terminal (it prompts for the token without echo), or pipe the token to `yojo login --service jira --base-url https://jira.example.test/jira --token-stdin`.",
    "details": {
      "service": "jira",
      "base_url": "https://jira.example.test/jira"
    }
  }
}
```

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`file_conflict`](errors.md#file_conflict), [`file_invalid`](errors.md#file_invalid), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 5 | [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`metadata_incomplete`](errors.md#metadata_incomplete), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

## `yojo agent print`

Print the yojo instructions for an AI agent: every command's signature and a --json example, plus the safety rules. Offline; paste the text into any chat.

```text
yojo agent print [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

None.

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes |
| `bytes` | integer | yes |
| `approx_tokens` | integer | yes |
| `commands` | integer | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo agent print
```

`data.text` is shortened here; the real text lists every command and is about 10 KB.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "text": "## yojo: Jira, Confluence, and Bitbucket Data Center\n\nUse `yojo` instead of calling the REST APIs. Each command below is complete: pick the one that\nfits the task and run it once. You do not need ...",
    "bytes": 10132,
    "approx_tokens": 2533,
    "commands": 28
  }
}
```

Error: an option the command does not take ([`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error), exit 2):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "usage_error",
    "message": "yojo: unrecognized arguments",
    "fix": "Use `yojo commands` to list commands.",
    "details": {
      "usage": "usage: yojo [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json] COMMAND ..."
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes**

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted) |

## `yojo agent install`

Write the agent instructions where each tool looks for them: agents (AGENTS.md), claude (.claude/skills/yojo/SKILL.md), cursor (.cursor/rules/yojo.mdc), copilot (.github/copilot-instructions.md), gemini (GEMINI.md). Only the marked yojo section is replaced; other text is kept, and an unchanged file is not rewritten.

```text
yojo agent install --target TARGET... [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `--target TARGET...` | array of one of `agents`, `claude`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `gemini` | yes | Repeat --target for each tool. |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `files` | array of objects | yes |
| `core_bytes` | integer | yes |
| `approx_tokens` | integer | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo agent install --target agents --target claude
```

Running it again changes nothing: an unchanged file is reported as `unchanged` and not rewritten. Text outside the marked yojo section is kept.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "files": [
      {
        "target": "agents",
        "path": "AGENTS.md",
        "action": "created",
        "managed_bytes": 10231
      },
      {
        "target": "claude",
        "path": ".claude/skills/yojo/SKILL.md",
        "action": "created",
        "managed_bytes": 10432
      }
    ],
    "core_bytes": 10132,
    "approx_tokens": 2533
  }
}
```

Error: AGENTS.md has a yojo:end marker line without a yojo:begin line ([`file_conflict`](errors.md#file_conflict), exit 2):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "file_conflict",

    "fix": "Edit /work/repo/AGENTS.md so it has one `<!-- yojo:begin ...-->` line followed by one `<!-- yojo:end -->` line, or remove both, then run the command again.",
    "details": {
      "path": "/work/repo/AGENTS.md",
      "begins": 0,
      "ends": 1
    }
  }
}
```

## `yojo jira issue create`

Create an issue of any type. Checks the project's live create screen and any yojo.yaml rules first, and refuses with every problem listed if anything is missing; nothing is written then.

```text
yojo jira issue create [PROJECT] [--type TYPE] [--summary TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--set NAME=VALUE...] [--input FILE] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | `PROJECT` | string | no | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `type` | `--type TYPE` | string | no | Issue type name, any case. |
| `summary` | `--summary TEXT` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `description` | `--description TEXT` | string | no | max length 32767 |
| `set` | `--set NAME=VALUE...` | array of strings | no | max items 100 |
| `input` | `--input FILE` | string | no | min length 1; Path to a UTF-8 JSON file, or '-' for stdin. |

**Input**

A JSON object from `--input PATH`, or from stdin with `--input -`. Unknown properties and duplicate keys are rejected. Where the command also has flags, the input is an alternative to them; a flag and an input property that disagree are refused.

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | no | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `type` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `summary` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `description` | string | no | max length 32767 |
| `fields` | object (field name to string or number or boolean or array of strings) | no | Field values keyed like --set NAME; same value forms, lists as arrays. |

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `status` | string or null | yes |
| `changed` | array of objects | yes |
| `issue_type` | string | yes |
| `project` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira issue create EXAMPLE --type Bug --summary 'Login button misaligned' --set Severity=Major --set 'Environment=Firefox 131 on Linux' --set Priority=High
```

Field names are the ones Jira shows (any case), yojo.yaml aliases, or raw IDs. The same call works with `--input -` and a JSON object instead of flags.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "key": "EXAMPLE-42",
    "url": "https://jira.example.test/jira/browse/EXAMPLE-42",
    "status": "To Do",
    "issue_type": "Bug",
    "project": "EXAMPLE",
    "changed": [
      {
        "field": "Summary",
        "id": "summary"
      },
      {
        "field": "Severity",
        "id": "customfield_10500"
      },
      {
        "field": "Environment",
        "id": "customfield_10600"
      },
      {
        "field": "Priority",
        "id": "priority"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## `yojo jira issue get`

Read an issue's key, summary, status, type, assignee, and link. --fields adds more fields by name; long text is trimmed unless --full.

```text
yojo jira issue get KEY [--fields NAMES] [--full] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `fields` | `--fields NAMES` | string | no | Comma-separated field names, aliases, or IDs. |
| `full` | `--full` | boolean | no | default `false`; Return long text without trimming. |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `summary` | string or null | yes |
| `status` | string or null | yes |
| `issue_type` | string or null | yes |
| `project` | string or null | yes |
| `assignee` | string or null | yes |
| `updated` | string or null | yes |
| `fields` | array of objects | yes |
| `more` | string or null | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira issue get EXAMPLE-42 --fields 'Story Points,priority'
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{

  "data": {

}
```

## `yojo jira issue update`

Change fields on an issue. Checks the live edit screen first, refuses with every problem listed, then reads the issue back to confirm the new values.

```text
yojo jira issue update KEY [--summary TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--set NAME=VALUE...] [--input FILE] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `summary` | `--summary TEXT` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `description` | `--description TEXT` | string | no | max length 32767 |
| `set` | `--set NAME=VALUE...` | array of strings | no | max items 100 |
| `input` | `--input FILE` | string | no | min length 1; Path to a UTF-8 JSON file, or '-' for stdin. |

**Input**

A JSON object from `--input PATH`, or from stdin with `--input -`. Unknown properties and duplicate keys are rejected. Where the command also has flags, the input is an alternative to them; a flag and an input property that disagree are refused.

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `summary` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `description` | string | no | max length 32767 |
| `fields` | object (field name to string or number or boolean or array of strings) | no | Field values keyed like --set NAME; same value forms, lists as arrays. |

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `status` | string or null | yes |
| `changed` | array of objects | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira issue update EXAMPLE-42 --set Priority=Highest --set 'Labels=login, ui'
```

Values are plain text: option, priority, and version names; usernames, display names, or emails; numbers; and comma-separated lists for multi-value fields. Every change is read back after the write.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,

        "field": "Priority",
        "id": "priority"
      },
      {
        "field": "Labels",
        "id": "labels"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## `yojo jira issue link`

Link two issues, for example `PROJ-1 blocks PROJ-2`. --type takes the link name or either direction's wording; the link is read back to confirm it.

```text
yojo jira issue link KEY OTHER_KEY --type LINK_TYPE [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `other` | `OTHER_KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `type` | `--type LINK_TYPE` | string | yes | Link type name or wording, e.g. Blocks, blocks, is blocked by. |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `relation` | string | yes |
| `other` | string | yes |
| `link_type` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira issue link EXAMPLE-42 EXAMPLE-43 --type blocks
```

## `yojo jira requirements`

Optional look-before-you-leap: every check `jira transition` would run for moving an issue to a status, plus the planned writes. Read-only.

```text
yojo jira requirements KEY --to STATUS [--set NAME=VALUE...] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `to` | `--to STATUS` | string | yes |   |
| `set` | `--set NAME=VALUE...` | array of strings | no | max items 100 |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `to` | string | yes |
| `from_status` | string | yes |
| `rule` | string or null | yes |
| `ready` | boolean | yes |
| `transition` | null or object | yes |
| `checks` | array of objects | yes |
| `plan` | object | yes |
| `notice` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira requirements EXAMPLE-42 --to 'In Progress'
```

Read-only. `--to` takes the destination status or the transition name, in any case.

Success (exit 0):

## `yojo jira transition`

Move an issue to a status (any case), setting transition-screen fields with --set. Checks every rule and required field first and refuses with all problems listed. A configured pre_edit runs a separate edit first and is not atomic.

```text
yojo jira transition KEY --to STATUS [--set NAME=VALUE...] [--input FILE] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `to` | `--to STATUS` | string | yes |   |
| `set` | `--set NAME=VALUE...` | array of strings | no | max items 100 |
| `input` | `--input FILE` | string | no | min length 1; Path to a UTF-8 JSON file, or '-' for stdin. |

**Input**

A JSON object from `--input PATH`, or from stdin with `--input -`. Unknown properties and duplicate keys are rejected. Where the command also has flags, the input is an alternative to them; a flag and an input property that disagree are refused.

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | object (field name to string or number or boolean or array of strings) | no | Field values keyed like --set NAME; same value forms, lists as arrays. |

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `from_status` | string | yes |
| `status` | string | yes |
| `transition_id` | string | yes |
| `changed` | array of objects | yes |
| `atomic` | boolean | yes |
| `operations` | array of objects | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira transition EXAMPLE-42 --to Done
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "key": "EXAMPLE-42",
    "url": "https://jira.example.test/jira/browse/EXAMPLE-42",
    "from_status": "In Progress",
    "status": "Done",
    "transition_id": "31",
    "changed": [],
    "atomic": true,
    "operations": [
      {
        "op": "transition",
        "method": "POST",
        "status": "succeeded",
        "fields": [],
        "transition_id": "31"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Error: no attachment matches the team's `{key}_Evidence_*` rule for Done; nothing is sent ([`requirements_unmet`](errors.md#requirements_unmet), exit 4):

```json
  "error": {
    "code": "requirements_unmet",

    "fix": "Apply each check's fix, then run details.retry (placeholders in <angle brackets> need your content).",
    "details": {
      "nothing_sent": true,
      "checks": [
        {
          "id": "attachment:{key}_Evidence_*",
          "status": "fail",

          "fix": "Attach a file whose name matches 'EXAMPLE-42_Evidence_*' with yojo jira attachment add EXAMPLE-42 --file '<file>'.",
          "details": {
            "pattern": "EXAMPLE-42_Evidence_*",
            "attachments": [
              "screenshot.png"
            ]
          }
        }
      ],
      "passed": 2,
      "key": "EXAMPLE-42",
      "to": "Done",
      "from_status": "In Progress",
      "retry": "yojo jira transition EXAMPLE-42 --to Done",
      "retry_argv": [
        "yojo",
        "jira",
        "transition",
        "EXAMPLE-42",
        "--to",
        "Done"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## `yojo jira attachment add`

Upload a file to an issue after checking permission and the size limit. Succeeds only when Jira confirms the uploaded name and size; otherwise outcome_unknown.

```text
yojo jira attachment add KEY --file FILE [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `file` | `--file FILE` | string | yes |   |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `attachments` | array of objects | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira attachment add EXAMPLE-42 --file EXAMPLE-42_Evidence_2026-10-24.xml
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "key": "EXAMPLE-42",
    "url": "https://jira.example.test/jira/browse/EXAMPLE-42",
    "attachments": [
      {
        "id": "10500",
        "filename": "EXAMPLE-42_Evidence_2026-10-24.xml",
        "size": 18432
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Error: a file larger than `jira.max_attachment_bytes`; nothing is sent ([`attachment_too_large`](errors.md#attachment_too_large), exit 2):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "attachment_too_large",
    "message": "EXAMPLE-42_Evidence_2026-10-24.xml is 2048 bytes; jira.max_attachment_bytes is 1024.",
    "fix": "Attach a smaller file (compress or split it), or raise jira.max_attachment_bytes in yojo.yaml if the team agrees.",
    "details": {
      "size": 2048,
      "limit": 1024
    }
  }
}
```

## `yojo jira comment add`

Add a plain-text comment from --body, a file, or stdin, after checking the issue exists and you may comment.

```text
yojo jira comment add KEY (--body TEXT | --body-file FILE) [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `KEY` | string | yes | pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*-[1-9][0-9]*(?![\s\S])` |
| `body` | `--body TEXT` | string | no | min length 1 |
| `body_file` | `--body-file FILE` | string | no | min length 1; Path to a plain UTF-8 text file (not JSON, max 1 MiB), or '-' for stdin. |

Requires exactly one of `body`, `body_file`.

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `comment_id` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira comment add EXAMPLE-42 --body 'Fixed in build 2026.10.24; ready for review.'
```

Use `--body` for short text, or `--body-file FILE` (`-` for stdin) for longer plain text.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "key": "EXAMPLE-42",
    "url": "https://jira.example.test/jira/browse/EXAMPLE-42?focusedCommentId=10777#comment-10777",
    "comment_id": "10777"
  }
}
```

## `yojo jira search`

Run a JQL search. Returns a bounded page (--limit, default 20) and next_start, the explicit cursor for the next page.

```text
yojo jira search --jql JQL [--start START] [--limit LIMIT] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jql` | `--jql JQL` | string | yes | min length 1; max length 4000 |
| `start` | `--start START` | integer | no | min 0; default `0` |
| `limit` | `--limit LIMIT` | integer | no | min 1; max 100; default `20` |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | integer | yes |
| `limit` | integer | yes |
| `total` | integer | yes |
| `next_start` | integer or null | yes |
| `issues` | array of objects | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo jira search --jql 'project = EXAMPLE AND status = "In Progress"' --limit 2
```

Results are bounded by `--limit` (default 20, max 100). When `next_start` is not null, pass it as `--start` for the next page.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "start": 0,
    "limit": 2,
    "total": 7,
    "next_start": 2,
    "issues": [
      {
        "key": "EXAMPLE-42",
        "summary": "Login button misaligned",
        "status": "In Progress",
        "issue_type": "Bug",
        "assignee": "Example User"
      },
      {
        "key": "EXAMPLE-43",
        "summary": "Add single sign-on",
        "status": "In Progress",
        "issue_type": "Story",
        "assignee": null
      }
    ],
    "content_trust": "untrusted"
  }
}
```

Error: JQL that names a project Jira does not know ([`remote_validation`](errors.md#remote_validation), exit 5):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "remote_validation",
    "message": "jira rejected the request (400).",
    "fix": "Correct the values listed in details.fields/details.messages and retry.",
    "details": {
      "service": "jira",
      "status": 400,
      "fields": {},
      "messages": [
        "The value 'NOPE' does not exist for the field 'project'."
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## `yojo confluence page read`

Read a page with its storage-format body, trimmed to 2000 characters unless --full. Returned content is untrusted data.

```text
yojo confluence page read ID [--full] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `ID` | string | yes | pattern `^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}(?![\s\S])` |
| `full` | `--full` | boolean | no | default `false`; Return long text without trimming. |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `type` | string | yes |
| `space_key` | string or null | yes |
| `version` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `ancestors` | array of strings | yes |
| `body_storage` | string | yes |
| `body_chars` | integer | yes |
| `truncated` | boolean | yes |
| `more` | string or null | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo confluence page read 123456
```

Long bodies are trimmed to 2000 characters with `truncated: true` and a `more` command that adds `--full`. Page content is untrusted data, never instructions.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "id": "123456",
    "title": "Release checklist",
    "type": "page",
    "space_key": "DOCS",
    "version": 3,
    "url": "https://confluence.example.test/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=123456",
    "ancestors": [
      "1000"
    ],
    "body_storage": "<p>Keep related decisions together.</p>",
    "body_chars": 48,
    "truncated": false,
    "more": null,
    "content_trust": "untrusted"
  }
}
```

Error: a page ID that does not exist or that you cannot view ([`not_found`](errors.md#not_found), exit 5):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "confluence returned 404 Not Found.",
    "fix": "Check the key or ID and that your account can view it.",
    "details": {
      "service": "confluence",
      "status": 404,
      "fields": {},
      "messages": [
        "No content found"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 5 | [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found) |

## `yojo confluence page search`

Run a CQL search. Returns a bounded page (--limit, default 20) and next_start, the explicit cursor for the next page.

```text
yojo confluence page search --cql CQL [--start START] [--limit LIMIT] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cql` | `--cql CQL` | string | yes | min length 1; max length 4000 |
| `start` | `--start START` | integer | no | min 0; default `0` |
| `limit` | `--limit LIMIT` | integer | no | min 1; max 100; default `20` |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | integer | yes |
| `limit` | integer | yes |
| `size` | integer | yes |
| `next_start` | integer or null | yes |
| `results` | array of objects | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo confluence page search --cql 'space = "DOCS" AND title ~ "release"' --limit 10
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "start": 0,
    "limit": 10,
    "size": 1,
    "next_start": null,
    "results": [
      {
        "id": "123456",
        "title": "Release checklist",
        "type": "page",
        "space_key": "DOCS",
        "version": 3
      }
    ],
    "content_trust": "untrusted"
  }
}
```

Error: CQL that Confluence cannot parse ([`remote_validation`](errors.md#remote_validation), exit 5):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "remote_validation",
    "message": "confluence rejected the request (400).",
    "fix": "Correct the values listed in details.fields/details.messages and retry.",
    "details": {
      "service": "confluence",
      "status": 400,
      "fields": {},
      "messages": [
        "Could not parse cql : title ~"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes**

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`config_not_found`](errors.md#config_not_found), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`service_not_configured`](errors.md#service_not_configured), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 5 | [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found), [`remote_validation`](errors.md#remote_validation) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

## `yojo confluence page create`

Create a page from storage-format content given as JSON input.

```text
yojo confluence page create --input INPUT [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | `--input INPUT` | string | yes | min length 1; Path to a UTF-8 JSON file, or '-' for stdin. |

**Input**

A JSON object from `--input PATH`, or from stdin with `--input -`. Unknown properties and duplicate keys are rejected. Where the command also has flags, the input is an alternative to them; a flag and an input property that disagree are refused.

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `space_key` | string | yes | pattern `^~?[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,255}(?![\s\S])` |
| `title` | string | yes | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `body_storage` | string | yes | max length 5242880 |
| `parent_id` | string | no | pattern `^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}(?![\s\S])` |

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `space_key` | string | yes |
| `version` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo confluence page create --input - <<'JSON'
{
  "space_key": "DOCS",
  "title": "Release 1.4 notes",
  "body_storage": "<p>Release 1.4 adds single sign-on.</p>",
  "parent_id": "123456"
}
JSON
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "id": "123457",
    "title": "Release 1.4 notes",
    "space_key": "DOCS",
    "version": 1,
    "url": "https://confluence.example.test/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=123457"
  }
}
```

Error: input without `body_storage`; rejected before any request ([`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), exit 2):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "input_invalid",
    "message": "The input does not match the confluence page create input schema.",
    "fix": "Correct the listed problems; see `yojo schema 'confluence page create'` (input).",
    "details": {
      "errors": [
        {
          "path": "/",
          "validator": "required",
          "missing": [
            "body_storage"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes**

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`config_not_found`](errors.md#config_not_found), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`service_not_configured`](errors.md#service_not_configured), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 4 | [`requirements_unmet`](errors.md#requirements_unmet) |
| 5 | [`conflict`](errors.md#conflict), [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found), [`remote_limit_exceeded`](errors.md#remote_limit_exceeded), [`remote_validation`](errors.md#remote_validation) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`metadata_incomplete`](errors.md#metadata_incomplete), [`outcome_unknown`](errors.md#outcome_unknown), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

## `yojo confluence page update`

Update a page's title and/or storage body. Requires expected_version and rejects stale versions. Succeeds only when Confluence confirms the page id, title, and next version; otherwise outcome_unknown.

```text
yojo confluence page update ID --input INPUT [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `ID` | string | yes | pattern `^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}(?![\s\S])` |
| `input` | `--input INPUT` | string | yes | min length 1; Path to a UTF-8 JSON file, or '-' for stdin. |

**Input**

A JSON object from `--input PATH`, or from stdin with `--input -`. Unknown properties and duplicate keys are rejected. Where the command also has flags, the input is an alternative to them; a flag and an input property that disagree are refused.

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expected_version` | integer | yes | min 1 |
| `title` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `body_storage` | string | no | max length 5242880 |

Requires at least one of `title`, `body_storage`.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `version` | integer | yes |
| `previous_version` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo confluence page update 123456 --input - <<'JSON'
{
  "expected_version": 3,
  "body_storage": "<p>Keep related decisions and links together.</p>"
}
JSON
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "id": "123456",
    "title": "Release checklist",
    "version": 4,
    "previous_version": 3,
    "url": "https://confluence.example.test/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=123456"
  }
}
```

Error: someone else saved version 4 after your `page read`; nothing is written ([`version_conflict`](errors.md#version_conflict), exit 5):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "version_conflict",
    "message": "Page 123456 is at version 4, not the expected version 3.",
    "fix": "Re-read the page with `yojo confluence page read 123456 --full`, merge your changes into the current content, and resubmit with expected_version 4.",
    "details": {
      "id": "123456",
      "expected_version": 3,
      "current_version": 4
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes**

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`config_not_found`](errors.md#config_not_found), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`service_not_configured`](errors.md#service_not_configured), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 4 | [`requirements_unmet`](errors.md#requirements_unmet) |
| 5 | [`conflict`](errors.md#conflict), [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found), [`remote_limit_exceeded`](errors.md#remote_limit_exceeded), [`remote_validation`](errors.md#remote_validation), [`version_conflict`](errors.md#version_conflict) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`metadata_incomplete`](errors.md#metadata_incomplete), [`outcome_unknown`](errors.md#outcome_unknown), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

## `yojo bitbucket repo list`

List repositories you can see, optionally in one project. Returns a bounded page (--limit, default 20) and next_start, Bitbucket's cursor for the next page.

```text
yojo bitbucket repo list [--project PROJECT] [--start START] [--limit LIMIT] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | `--project PROJECT` | string | no | pattern `^~?[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,127}(?![\s\S])` |
| `start` | `--start START` | integer | no | min 0; default `0` |
| `limit` | `--limit LIMIT` | integer | no | min 1; max 100; default `20` |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `project` | string or null | yes |
| `start` | integer | yes |
| `limit` | integer | yes |
| `next_start` | integer or null | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |
| `repos` | array of objects | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo bitbucket repo list --project PROJ
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "project": "PROJ",
    "start": 0,
    "limit": 20,
    "next_start": 2,
    "repos": [
      {
        "repo": "PROJ/web",
        "name": "web",
        "url": "https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/web/browse"
      },
      {
        "repo": "PROJ/api",
        "name": "api",
        "url": "https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/api/browse"
      }
    ],
    "content_trust": "untrusted"
  }
}
```

Error: Bitbucket answers a page that is not the last one without a usable `nextPageStart`; yojo refuses to guess the next cursor ([`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), exit 6):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "response_invalid",
    "message": "Bitbucket returned a repository list page without a usable next cursor, so the list cannot continue safely.",
    "fix": "Run the command again. If it repeats, narrow it (a smaller --limit, or --filter for branches) and check that no proxy rewrites Bitbucket responses.",
    "details": {
      "what": "repository list page",
      "start": 0
    }
  }
}
```

| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |

| `state` | `--state OPEN|MERGED|DECLINED|ALL` | one of `OPEN`, `MERGED`, `DECLINED`, `ALL` | no | default `OPEN` |
| `start` | `--start START` | integer | no | min 0; default `0` |
| `limit` | `--limit LIMIT` | integer | no | min 1; max 100; default `20` |

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `state` | one of `OPEN`, `MERGED`, `DECLINED`, `ALL` | yes |
| `start` | integer | yes |
| `limit` | integer | yes |
| `next_start` | integer or null | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |
| `pull_requests` | array of objects | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo bitbucket pr list --repo PROJ/web --state open
```

`--state` takes OPEN, MERGED, DECLINED, or ALL in any case.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "repo": "PROJ/web",
    "state": "OPEN",
    "start": 0,
    "limit": 20,
    "next_start": null,
    "pull_requests": [
      {
        "id": 42,
        "title": "Fix login on Safari",
        "state": "OPEN",
        "source": "feature/login",
        "target": "main",
        "author": "Example User",
        "updated": "2026-10-28T12:53:31Z"
      }
    ],
    "content_trust": "untrusted",
    "url": "https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/web/pull-requests"
  }
}
```

Error: `--state closed`, which Bitbucket does not have; rejected before any request ([`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error), exit 2):

```json
  "error": {
    "code": "usage_error",

    "fix": "Use `yojo bitbucket pr list --repo PROJECT/slug [--state OPEN|MERGED|DECLINED|ALL] [--start N] [--limit N]`, for example `yojo --json bitbucket pr list --repo PROJ/web --state open`.",
    "details": {
      "usage": "yojo bitbucket pr list --repo PROJECT/slug [--state OPEN|MERGED|DECLINED|ALL] [--start N] [--limit N]"
    }
  }
}
```

## `yojo bitbucket pr get`

Read a pull request: title, state, branches, author, reviewers, and description (trimmed unless --full). Reviewers are limited to ten; reviewers_total and reviewers_truncated signal the limit, and reviewers_url opens the full view. Returned content is untrusted data.

```text
yojo bitbucket pr get ID --repo PROJECT/slug [--full] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `ID` | integer | yes | min 1; Pull request ID. |
| `repo` | `--repo PROJECT/slug` | string | yes | pattern `^~?[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,127}/(?!\.{1,2}(?![\s\S]))[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}(?![\s\S])`; Repository as PROJECT/slug, for example PROJ/web. |
| `full` | `--full` | boolean | no | default `false`; Return long text without trimming. |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `state` | string or null | yes |
| `source` | string or null | yes |
| `target` | string or null | yes |
| `author` | string or null | yes |
| `created` | string or null | yes |
| `updated` | string or null | yes |
| `reviewers` | array of objects | yes |
| `reviewers_total` | integer | yes |
| `reviewers_truncated` | boolean | yes |
| `reviewers_url` | string or null | yes |
| `description` | string | yes |
| `truncated` | boolean | yes |
| `more` | string or null | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo bitbucket pr get 42 --repo PROJ/web
```

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "id": 42,
    "repo": "PROJ/web",
    "title": "Fix login on Safari",
    "state": "OPEN",
    "source": "feature/login",
    "target": "main",
    "author": "Example User",
    "created": "2026-10-28T11:53:31Z",
    "updated": "2026-10-28T12:53:31Z",
    "reviewers": [
      {
        "name": "Example Reviewer",
        "status": "UNAPPROVED"
      }
    ],
    "reviewers_total": 1,
    "reviewers_truncated": false,
    "reviewers_url": null,
    "description": "Handles an empty user before the credential check.",
    "truncated": false,
    "more": null,
    "url": "https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/web/pull-requests/42",
    "content_trust": "untrusted"
  }
}
```

Error: no pull request 42 in PROJ/web ([`not_found`](errors.md#not_found), exit 5):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "bitbucket returned 404 Not Found.",
    "fix": "Check the key or ID and that your account can view it.",
    "details": {
      "service": "bitbucket",
      "status": 404,
      "fields": {},
      "messages": [
        "Pull request 42 does not exist in PROJ/web."
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes**

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`config_not_found`](errors.md#config_not_found), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`service_not_configured`](errors.md#service_not_configured), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 5 | [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

## `yojo bitbucket pr diff`

Show a pull request's changes as a unified diff with a list of changed files. Trimmed to about 2000 characters and 10 files unless --full; --path FILE shows one file (add --old-path OLD for a renamed file). complete is false whenever yojo or Bitbucket cut anything. more, when set, is a yojo command that may show more; inspect, when set, is a git command for what Bitbucket would not return.

```text
yojo bitbucket pr diff ID --repo PROJECT/slug [--path FILE] [--old-path FILE] [--full] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `ID` | integer | yes | min 1; Pull request ID. |
| `repo` | `--repo PROJECT/slug` | string | yes | pattern `^~?[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,127}/(?!\.{1,2}(?![\s\S]))[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}(?![\s\S])`; Repository as PROJECT/slug, for example PROJ/web. |
| `path` | `--path FILE` | string | no | min length 1; max length 1024; Repository-relative file path, e.g. src/app.py. |
| `old_path` | `--old-path FILE` | string | no | min length 1; max length 1024; The file's path before a rename or copy; needs path. |
| `full` | `--full` | boolean | no | default `false`; Return long text without trimming. |

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `path` | string or null | yes |
| `files_total` | integer | yes |
| `files` | array of objects | yes |
| `diff` | string | yes |
| `diff_chars` | integer | yes |
| `truncated` | boolean | yes |
| `server_truncated` | boolean | yes |
| `truncated_files` | array of strings | yes |
| `complete` | boolean | yes |
| `more` | string or null | yes |
| `inspect` | string or null | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |
| `content_trust` | constant `untrusted` | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo bitbucket pr diff 42 --repo PROJ/web --path src/app.py
```

Without `--path` the whole pull request is shown, trimmed unless `--full`. `complete` is false whenever yojo or Bitbucket cut anything. `more`, when set, is a yojo command that may show more; `inspect`, when set, is a git command for what Bitbucket would not return.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "id": 42,
    "repo": "PROJ/web",
    "path": "src/app.py",
    "files_total": 1,
    "files": [
      {
        "path": "src/app.py",
        "old_path": null,
        "change": "modified",
        "added": 2,
        "removed": 1
      }
    ],
    "diff": "diff --git a/src/app.py b/src/app.py\n--- a/src/app.py\n+++ b/src/app.py\n@@ -10,2 +10,3 @@\n def login(user):\n-    return check(user)\n+    if not user:\n+        return False\n",
    "diff_chars": 171,
    "truncated": false,
    "server_truncated": false,
    "truncated_files": [],
    "complete": true,
    "more": null,
    "inspect": null,
    "url": "https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/web/pull-requests/42/diff#src/app.py",
    "content_trust": "untrusted"
  }
}
```

Error: a `--path` that leaves the repository; rejected before any request ([`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error), exit 2):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "usage_error",
    "message": "yojo bitbucket pr diff: argument --path: must be a repository-relative file path such as src/a.py",
    "fix": "Use `yojo bitbucket pr diff ID --repo PROJECT/slug [--path FILE [--old-path FILE]] [--full]`, for example `yojo --json bitbucket pr diff 42 --repo PROJ/web --path src/app.py`.",
    "details": {
      "usage": "yojo bitbucket pr diff ID --repo PROJECT/slug [--path FILE [--old-path FILE]] [--full]"
    }
  }
}
```

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`config_not_found`](errors.md#config_not_found), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`service_not_configured`](errors.md#service_not_configured), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 5 | [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

## `yojo bitbucket pr create`

Open a pull request between two branches of one repository. Checks the repository, both branches, the title, and for an open pull request with the same branches first, and refuses with every problem listed; nothing is written then.

```text
yojo bitbucket pr create [--repo PROJECT/slug] [--source BRANCH] [--target BRANCH] [--title TEXT] [--description TEXT] [--input FILE] [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `--repo PROJECT/slug` | string | no | pattern `^~?[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,127}/(?!\.{1,2}(?![\s\S]))[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}(?![\s\S])`; Repository as PROJECT/slug, for example PROJ/web. |
| `source` | `--source BRANCH` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255; Branch name in the same repository, e.g. feature/login or refs/heads/main. |
| `target` | `--target BRANCH` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255; Branch name in the same repository, e.g. feature/login or refs/heads/main. |
| `title` | `--title TEXT` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `description` | `--description TEXT` | string | no | max length 32767 |
| `input` | `--input FILE` | string | no | min length 1; Path to a UTF-8 JSON file, or '-' for stdin. |

**Input**

A JSON object from `--input PATH`, or from stdin with `--input -`. Unknown properties and duplicate keys are rejected. Where the command also has flags, the input is an alternative to them; a flag and an input property that disagree are refused.

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | no | pattern `^~?[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,127}/(?!\.{1,2}(?![\s\S]))[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}(?![\s\S])` |
| `source` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255; Branch name in the same repository, e.g. feature/login or refs/heads/main. |
| `target` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255; Branch name in the same repository, e.g. feature/login or refs/heads/main. |
| `title` | string | no | min length 1; max length 255 |
| `description` | string | no | max length 32767 |

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `title` | string | yes |
| `source` | string | yes |
| `target` | string | yes |
| `state` | string or null | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo bitbucket pr create --input - <<'JSON'
{
  "repo": "PROJ/web",
  "source": "feature/login",
  "target": "main",
  "title": "Fix login on Safari",
  "description": "Handles an empty user before the credential check."
}
JSON
```

Flags are the usual form: `yojo bitbucket pr create --repo PROJ/web --source feature/login --target main --title '...'`. `--input -` reads the same names as JSON, useful for a long description; a value given both ways must match.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "id": 42,
    "repo": "PROJ/web",
    "title": "Fix login on Safari",
    "source": "feature/login",
    "target": "main",
    "state": "OPEN",
    "url": "https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/web/pull-requests/42"
  }
}
```

Error: a misspelled source branch and no title, given as flags; every problem is listed and nothing is sent ([`requirements_unmet`](errors.md#requirements_unmet), exit 4):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "requirements_unmet",
    "message": "Opening a pull request in PROJ/web was refused with 3 problem(s); nothing was sent.",
    "fix": "Apply each check's fix, then run details.retry (placeholders in <angle brackets> need your content).",
    "details": {
      "nothing_sent": true,
      "checks": [
        {
          "id": "title",
          "status": "fail",
          "message": "The title is missing or blank.",
          "fix": "Add --title 'one-line title'."
        },
        {
          "id": "source",
          "status": "fail",
          "message": "No branch 'feature/logn' in PROJ/web. Did you mean 'feature/login'?",
          "fix": "Use 'feature/login'. List branches with `yojo bitbucket branch list --repo PROJ/web --filter feature/logn`.",
          "details": {
            "given": "feature/logn",
            "kind": "not_found",
            "suggestion": "feature/login"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "duplicate",
          "status": "unverified",
          "message": "Open pull requests cannot be checked until the repository and both branches are known.",
          "fix": "Resolve the repo, source, and target checks first."
        }
      ],
      "passed": 2,
      "retry": "yojo bitbucket pr create --repo PROJ/web --source feature/login --target main --title '<title>'",
      "retry_argv": [
        "yojo",
        "bitbucket",
        "pr",
        "create",
        "--repo",
        "PROJ/web",
        "--source",
        "feature/login",
        "--target",
        "main",
        "--title",
        "<title>"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes**

| Exit | Error codes |
|------|-------------|
| 2 | [`config_invalid`](errors.md#config_invalid), [`config_legacy`](errors.md#config_legacy), [`config_not_found`](errors.md#config_not_found), [`input_invalid`](errors.md#input_invalid), [`service_not_configured`](errors.md#service_not_configured), [`usage_error`](errors.md#usage_error) |
| 3 | [`auth_failed`](errors.md#auth_failed), [`auth_missing`](errors.md#auth_missing), [`forbidden`](errors.md#forbidden), [`keyring_unavailable`](errors.md#keyring_unavailable) |
| 4 | [`requirements_unmet`](errors.md#requirements_unmet) |
| 5 | [`conflict`](errors.md#conflict), [`not_found`](errors.md#not_found), [`remote_limit_exceeded`](errors.md#remote_limit_exceeded), [`remote_validation`](errors.md#remote_validation) |
| 6 | [`internal_error`](errors.md#internal_error), [`interrupted`](errors.md#interrupted), [`metadata_incomplete`](errors.md#metadata_incomplete), [`outcome_unknown`](errors.md#outcome_unknown), [`rate_limited`](errors.md#rate_limited), [`redirect_refused`](errors.md#redirect_refused), [`response_invalid`](errors.md#response_invalid), [`service_error`](errors.md#service_error), [`tls_error`](errors.md#tls_error), [`transport_error`](errors.md#transport_error) |

## `yojo bitbucket pr comment`

Add a plain-text comment to a pull request from --body, a file, or stdin, after checking the pull request exists and has no identical comment.

```text
yojo bitbucket pr comment ID --repo PROJECT/slug (--body TEXT | --body-file FILE) [--config PATH] [--base-url URL] [--json]
```

**Arguments**

| Argument | CLI | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `ID` | integer | yes | min 1; Pull request ID. |
| `repo` | `--repo PROJECT/slug` | string | yes | pattern `^~?[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,127}/(?!\.{1,2}(?![\s\S]))[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}(?![\s\S])`; Repository as PROJECT/slug, for example PROJ/web. |
| `body` | `--body TEXT` | string | no | min length 1 |
| `body_file` | `--body-file FILE` | string | no | min length 1; Path to a plain UTF-8 text file (not JSON, max 1 MiB), or '-' for stdin. |

Requires exactly one of `body`, `body_file`.

**Input**

No JSON input.

**Output**

Success `data` fields:

| Field | Type | Always present |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |
| `repo` | string | yes |
| `comment_id` | integer | yes |
| `url` | string | yes |

**Example**

```bash
yojo bitbucket pr comment 42 --repo PROJ/web --body 'Ready for review.'
```

Use `--body` for short text, or `--body-file FILE` (`-` for stdin) for longer plain text.

Success (exit 0):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "id": 42,
    "repo": "PROJ/web",
    "comment_id": 777,
    "url": "https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/web/pull-requests/42/overview?commentId=777"
  }
}
```

Error: the pull request already has a comment with exactly this text; nothing is sent ([`requirements_unmet`](errors.md#requirements_unmet), exit 4):

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "requirements_unmet",
    "message": "Commenting on pull request #42 was refused with 1 problem(s); nothing was sent.",

      "checks": [
        {

          "fix": "Nothing to send if it is yours (see https://bitbucket.example.test/bitbucket/projects/PROJ/repos/web/pull-requests/42/overview); to add something new, change the text.",
          "details": {
            "comment_id": 501
          }
        }
      ],
      "passed": 1,
      "retry": null,
      "retry_argv": null
    }
  }
}
```
